metadata.title: The Lid: A Geometric Framework for the Riemann Hypothesis via Winding Numbers, Canonical Boundaries, and Energy Minimization
metadata.description: We introduce the Lid equation — a winding-number formulation of the Riemann Hypothesis — and derive four supporting theorems: The Lid (T1), the Fingerprint Theorem (T2), the Arc Theorem (T3), and the Canonical Boundary Principle (T4 / CBP). CBP identifies Fix(σ), the fixed set of the antiholomorphic involution σ(s)=1−s̄, as the unique canonical boundary for ζ. The edge scan (§11) confirms a perfectly sharp winding-number jump at Re(s)=1/2 with no pre-jump plateau to Δσ=10⁻⁴. Antoine's Completeness Theorem (§12, DERIVED) establishes W(σ>1/2)=−1 ↔ RH via argument principle and functional equation. The energy functional (§15) reformulates RH as minimization of E=Σ(Re(ρ)−1/2)², showing Fix(σ) is the maximum-symmetry ground state. All numerical results consistent with RH to stated precision. Related preprint: Young-Laplace Kun Framework, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22896946.
metadata.notes: Preprint. Code and results at https://github.com/OrdersOfMagnitudeLLC/type1-toolkit. Numerical verification via Devin AI.
